summary: Proof of concept on the rollo toy set with the BatchNorm MLP encoder, 30 seeds, rules pre-registered before each run (Notebooks/PoC_Hypotheses_Rollo.ipynb, run 3). Task-level adaptation is supported; attention with consensus down-weights artifact-like contamination; the local term (K2) shows no gain and the K3 ladder is ordered as expected but not significant. Toy-set results: task, K1 and K2 approved; K3 partly approved (consensus yes, combining terms no). EEG experiments have not run.

hypotheses.statement: Contaminated windows receive less attention weight than clean ones, more so than without consensus.
hypotheses.metric: attention-mass contrast c on contaminated vs clean windows
hypotheses.criterion: pre-registered rule: every contrast of the family with (Holm-adjusted) p < 0.05
hypotheses.rationale: Corrected test (L115): v55 K1 is about marked (artifact) windows; on artifact contamination both K1a (marked < clean) and K1b (MIL-CREDA > no-consensus) pass at every rate (Holm). Donor-class contamination is outside the claim and is reported as information on the r38 consensus assumption (fails at 10%). Scope: toy set (rollo, BatchNorm MLP); EEG verdict pending in the full experiments.

hypotheses.statement: The local term aligns each target bag with its compatible source partner beyond the global term.
hypotheses.criterion: pre-registered rule: every contrast of the family with (Holm-adjusted) p < 0.05
hypotheses.observed: Push toward own partner: TGL 0.119 vs TG 0.053 (clean, 30 seeds); K2a p_Holm<1e-8, K2b p_Holm<1e-7 (HL 0.067). Room gate held (ratio 1.05, source acc 0.93). Information: end margin own-vs-others TGL -0.040 vs TG -0.046 (n.s.).
hypotheses.rationale: Approved on the toy set: with a subject-specific residual the global term cannot remove, the local term pushes each target bag toward its own source partner more than the global term alone. It does not sharpen the own-vs-others margin beyond TG. Scope: toy set (rollo, BatchNorm MLP, subject-specific residual scenario, run 6); EEG verdict pending in the full experiments.

hypotheses.statement: Both adaptation terms together beat each alone, and the consensus beats its no-consensus variant.
hypotheses.criterion: pre-registered rule: every contrast of the family with (Holm-adjusted) p < 0.05
hypotheses.observed: K3a (consensus, 40% artifacts): TGL 0.750 vs TGL-NC 0.725, p=0.032. Ablation: clean TGL 0.760, TG 0.754, TL 0.741 (K3b p_Holm 0.40, K3c 0.25); artifact TGL 0.750, TG 0.751, TL 0.757 (p_Holm 1.0).
hypotheses.rationale: Partly approved on the toy set: the consensus term improves accuracy under 40% artifact contamination (K3a); combining the global and local terms does not improve accuracy over either alone (K3b, K3c), although the local term does move bags toward their partners (H-K2). Scope: toy set (rollo, BatchNorm MLP, subject-specific residual scenario, run 6); EEG verdict pending in the full experiments.

qualitative.title: Attention under artifact contamination
qualitative.reading: Artifacts receive less weight than clean windows at every rate.

limitations: Toy-set evidence only; no EEG campaign has run.
Comparators are not part of the PoC, so ranking claims are untested here.
next_steps: Discuss K2 and K3 before the full EEG run.
Place the full run with the timing probe and plan before launching.

novelty.claim: Unsupervised bag-level adaptation of subject-level EEG diagnosis to unlabeled target bags (relevance- and consensus-weighted bag kernel, class-conditional Rényi global alignment, subject-level local alignment).
novelty.rationale: On the toy set the method adapts beyond the BN-matched source-only floor, its consensus attention down-weights artifacts, and its local term pulls bags toward their own partner under a subject-specific residual; combining the two alignment terms gives no accuracy gain, and the comparison against the eight comparators is left to the EEG experiments.
